artworks.title: The Banquet of Achelous
artworks.artist: Peter Paul Rubens and Jan Brueghel the Elder
artworks.description: Metropolitan Museum collaboration: Achelous hosts Theseus at a grotto feast and recounts the wrestling for Deianira — Ovid's Metamorphoses banquet where the broken horn spills as cornucopia and the Nessus tragedy waits in the telling.

artworks.title: Nessus and Deianira
artworks.description: Simonet's academic canvas: the centaur seizes Deianira at the Evenus — the dying deceit Achelous' feast narrative will name as the shirt that kills Heracles.

artworks.title: Heracles, Deianira and Nessus (Attic black-figure hydria, Louvre E 803)
artworks.artist: Attributed to the Painter of Vatican 309
artworks.description: Louvre E 803: the river-crossing confrontation that seeds the poisoned 'love-charm' — the feast's dark punchline already painted in sixth-century black-figure.

artworks.title: Hercules and Deianira (Pompeian fresco)
artworks.description: Pompeian wall painting of the conjugal pair whose story Achelous recounts at his harvest feast — the serene face of the wife who will send the fatal tunic.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book 9: Achelous at his own harvest feast narrates the wrestling for Deianira, Nessus' lie, and the shirt that will kill Heracles — Ovid's inset tragedy.

popCulture.title: Trachiniae
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' Women of Trachis — the poisoned robe and Deianira's fatal gift remain the stage version of the feast's dark punchline.

popCulture.title: Deianira
popCulture.description: The wife who meant to keep love and sent death — her name stays bound to Nessus' blood and Heracles' last agony.
